his_text: Generate ground truth by injecting specified failure modes at specified severities into real trajectories, and evaluate monitor fidelity on these synthetic attacks.
Have the monitor output a severity score on a one-to-ten scale and let a user-chosen threshold convert that score into a block-or-approve decision.
Let the monitor model judge each action's risk in context rather than relying on a deterministic rule set, since fixed rules cannot cover varied deployments.
Give the monitor the full trajectory context with tool call outputs removed when evaluating and selecting a configuration.
Keep the monitoring prompt long and detailed rather than compressing it, and offset the added cost with caching.
Pair a fast triage model with a stronger gateway model for the default, and raise the triage threshold plus a mid-tier gateway for the lighter tier.
Validate the generation pipeline's attack and severity labels against a human-annotated set of attack steps, iterating the rubric on disagreements.
Require the monitor to output an integer suspicion score on a one-to-ten scale rather than a binary flag for each reviewed trajectory.
Stop human-guided prompt refinement after a predeclared limit of three iterations, even though further refinement cycles remain possible in principle on both datasets.
Treat the single significant gain as an isolated exception and conclude overall that monitor performance is largely saturated at the simple prompt-sweep stage.
Exclude trajectories where the assigned side task was not completed from the test set, labeling only those with verified side-task success as scheming.
Include a small panel of capable monitor models across multiple providers and drop the two most expensive candidates rather than evaluating every frontier option.
Present two competing explanations, a narrow or artifact-heavy synthetic training distribution versus fundamental limits of prompt optimization, and propose future work for each.
Scan agent logs for tasks with very low success across all agents and relatively higher failure rates for stronger agents, then use those patterns to flag flaws.
Manually check every task the automated judges flag and accept flags only after human verification, then exclude validated tasks and recompute the final metric.
State that analyzing agent behavior logs is necessary for evaluation validity while explicitly denying that log analysis alone is sufficient for trustworthy evaluation.
Build commercial monitoring and control products for AI coding agents while continuing the organization's established core safety research work in parallel.
Pursue safety monitoring as the most obvious fit for a commercial safety product, while noting that this expectation has not yet been validated in practice.
Treat most AI governance work as unsuitable for for-profit ventures, keeping it instead in non-profits or small insulated teams inside larger organizations.
Stop a given grant program when its metrics keep getting goodharted, taking persistent gaming as negative evidence that the program should end altogether.
Require the funder and applicant to agree upfront on a scaling condition, by default a plot of money spent against a safety proxy, before releasing more money.
Prioritize safety monitoring as the grant program's lead research direction over other candidate areas, where scaling the work is expected to have high returns.
Fund automated conceptual alignment research despite likely early failures, while shutting down any projects that would differentially accelerate capabilities.
Announce the open grant program publicly now rather than waiting until detailed theses about which areas are concretely fundable have been fully worked out.
Show each guardrail would have caught the real failures seen in the past and withstand agents actively trying to circumvent it.
Run SFT then RL on the main model family and SFT-only on the other families, since the refinement step adds cost for a smaller gain.
Pick the frontier model whose rationales and scores best match ground truth on a held-out set under the behavior specification.
Describe broader behavioral coverage as crucial overall despite non-monotonic gains, presenting the intermediate regression alongside final results.
Optimize the prompted baselines over several prompt variants and report the best, which is the team's full behavior specification prompt.
Filter out the low-scoring rationales and class-balance the remaining dataset so benign and misaligned samples appear in equal numbers.
Use every filtered sample at the largest size rather than equal per-stratum sampling, keeping only the within-source class balance.
Set each checkpoint's training context window to its standard native length and do not use extended-context capabilities.
Read the increase in false positives as training widening the monitor's suspicion, so that ordinary mistakes and incompetence in trajectories get flagged as scheming.
